title: customer-edge-onboarding-responsibility-matrix-2026
author: Aisha Gomez
body:
Overview:

This page defines a clear, role-based responsibility matrix and an actionable checklist for onboarding customers running Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) with an emphasis on edge or branch-site scenarios. The goal is to reduce handoff ambiguity during pre-install, installation, and day-2 operations, and to make acceptance criteria for SLA and operational readiness explicit.

Scope:
- Applies to Redwood Private deployments in VPC-connected customer networks and small-footprint edge/on-prem sites.
- Covers network, hardware, security, telemetry, operator access, upgrade/rollback responsibilities, and acceptance tests.
- Not a replacement for the full operator runbook — see related pages for detailed operator procedures.

Key audiences:
- Customer cloud/network/security/platform teams
- Redwood Field Engineering and Solutions (Field Ops)
- Redwood Platform & Private Deployments engineering

High-level responsibilities (RACI-style summary):
- R = Responsible (does the work), A = Accountable, C = Consulted, I = Informed

| Area | Customer | Redwood Field Ops | Redwood Platform Eng | Notes |
|------|----------|-------------------|----------------------|-------|
| Network provisioning (VPC/subnets, NAT, route tables) | R/A | C | I | Customer implements; Field Ops validates connectivity and egress paths. |
| Firewall / perimeter rules | R/A | C | I | Customer owns perimeter; Redwood provides recommended rule set. |
| Host/Tenant identity & service accounts | R | C | I | Customer creates service accounts and keys; Redwood documents principle-of-least-privilege bindings. |
| KMS/HSM integration & key partitioning | R | C | C | Customer manages keys; Redwood provides integration steps and test vectors. |
| Image deployment and attestation | R/A (on-prem) | C | C | Customer pulls signed images; Field Ops guides attestation. |
| Operator access & bastion configuration | R | R/A | C | Customer provides jump hosts; Field Ops requires specified access windows for installs. |
| Telemetry & metrics collection (sampling rates) | R/C | R | C | Customer chooses telemetry egress policy; Redwood recommends sampling & retention defaults. |
| Routine upgrades / model swaps | C | R/A | R | Redwood Platform owns upgrade tooling; Field Ops coordinates with customer windows. |
| Emergency rollback | R (approve) | R | R/A | Platform owns rollback artifacts and evidence capture; customer authorizes failback. |

Pre-install checklist (customer deliverables):
1) Network & routing
   - VPC/subnet allocation for control plane and data plane (minimum two subnets: control and runtime)
   - Security group rules: allow outbound TLS to Redwood control plane endpoints; restrict inbound to operator bastion only
   - Minimum MTU and no UDP fragmentation across path for large model artifact transfers

2) DNS and certificate expectations
   - Customer-managed wildcard DNS entries (or split-horizon DNS) for local endpoints if required
   - TLS termination strategy documented (customer TLS vs Redwood-managed TLS)

3) KMS/HSM & secret management
   - Customer KMS endpoints and principal to be supplied (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP Cloud KMS, or on-prem HSM)
   - Key wrapping policy and rotation windows (recommended quarterly rotation for field deployments)

4) Host inventory & hardware readiness (on-prem/edge)
   - CPU/GPU family and driver versions, memory, NVMe sizing, per-host power budget
   - IPMI/BMC or out-of-band management access for operator automation

5) Operator access & maintenance windows
   - Pre-authorized operator accounts (SSH/SSO) and emergency contact list
   - Recurring maintenance windows and blackout windows defined

Minimum network and performance thresholds (acceptance criteria):
- Control plane egress latency: <= 120 ms to Redwood control endpoints (measured p95)
- Data-plane RTT for common customer region: p95 <= 80 ms for VPC-local traffic; for edge sites, acceptable p95 <= 150 ms with documented burst allowances
- Sustained throughput for model artifact download: >= 200 Mbps per host during initial sync (or provide an operational schedule)
- Packet loss: < 0.5% p99 across measured paths during acceptance tests

Telemetry & observability contract:
- Telemetry classes:
  - Essential: service health metrics (uptime, architecture state transitions), error rates, token-level cost counters
  - Optional: detailed trace spans, kernel metrics, GPU telemetry (smoothed)
- Customer options:
  - Push to Redwood consolidator (recommended for hosted telemetry) OR
  - Push to customer collector with a Redfish-compatible subset (for privacy-sensitive sites)
- Sampling guidance:
  - Default: 1:10 for traces, 1:100 for GPU per-replication counters; increase during incident drills

Acceptance test suite (smoke + perf) — operator and customer responsibilities:
1) Connectivity smoke (Field Ops executes, Customer provides network view)
   - From operator bastion run: curl -v https://<local-endpoint>/healthz
   - Expected: 200 OK within 500ms and JSON health payload with component statuses

2) Model load and inference smoke (joint)
   - Pull a small reference model artifact (sha256 verified) and load into runtime; run n=100 single-token generation requests
   - Expected: average single-token latency < 120ms for small model profile; no errors > 1%

3) KV cache and prefix-caching validation (joint)
   - Run repeated session with context reuse and validate that subsequent calls have p50 latency delta < 20ms vs first call

4) Telemetry ingestion and retention verification (Customer validates local retention settings)

Upgrade & rollback boundaries (operational contract):
- Redwood Platform Eng provides a release manifest and compatibility matrix 14 days before a non-emergency upgrade.
- Field Ops coordinates canary windows and notifies customer operators at least 7 days before scheduled canary.
- Customer must approve production cutover within 48 hours of canary completion.
- Rollback policy:
  - Automatic safe-rollback if error budget breach > 2x configured SLO for 30m continuous window during rollout
  - For stateful changes (KV format or model remapping) full rollback requires Customer sign-off and snapshot evidence

Example operator commands (smoke tests):
- Health check (bash):
  curl -sSf -H 'Authorization: Bearer <OP_TOKEN>' https://local-redwood.example.com/healthz | jq .

- Artifact verify (bash):
  sha256sum downloaded/model.tar.gz | grep <expected-sha256>

Operator-runbook excerpt: emergency rollback decision flow (short):
1) Detect: increase in 5xx rate > 3x baseline OR latency p99 > SLO by 2x for 20m -> trigger incident bridge and page Field Ops lead
2) Contain: apply traffic-shed to fallback model variant and isolate partial rollout group
3) Evaluate: collect traces, traces sampling ramp, and artifact digests; prepare evidence bundle
4) Rollback: Redwood Platform initiates artifact revert; Field Ops coordinates customer traffic steering; Customer approves cutback where stateful snapshots are required
5) Postmortem: produce incident report within 72 hours with RCA and suggested rollout gating changes

Communication & handoff templates:
- Pre-install email (example):
  Subject: Redwood Private install window - action items and operator access
  Body: Please provide (1) SSH key for operator user, (2) pre-authorized KMS principal ARN, (3) maintenance window on MM/DD 00:00-04:00 UTC. We will perform connectivity validation and initial artifact sync.

Related acceptance artifacts to deliver to customer during handoff:
- Signed image digests and attestation log
- Telemetry sampling & retention policy in writing
- Final responsibility matrix snapshot and operator contact list

Appendix: Quick acceptance checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Network subnets provisioned and routes validated
- [ ] Operator bastion access supplied and tested
- [ ] KMS principal created and test encrypt/decrypt executed
- [ ] At least one host with required GPU driver & NVMe available
- [ ] Signed image digest verified by Field Ops
- [ ] Telemetry endpoint validated and retention policy applied
- [ ] Canary upgrade window scheduled and approved

If there are questions about any of the items above, contact Field Ops (field-ops@redwood.ai) or the Private Deployments engineering owner (eng-private@redwood.ai).
